subject: Geography
sub_topic: Time zones and international date line

concepts.name: Prime Meridian (0° Longitude): Basis and Significance
key_dimensions: Historical establishment at Greenwich, London and the 1884 International Meridian Conference
Distinction between astronomical/geographic Prime Meridian and the IERS Reference Meridian (102m east due to GPS)
Role as the reference for calculating all world time zones (GMT/UTC)
Difference between GMT (astronomical) and UTC (atomic clock-based) — UPSC trap on interchangeable use

concepts.name: Structure of Standard Time Zones: 24-Zone System
key_dimensions: Theoretical division of Earth into 24 zones of 15° longitude each (1 hour = 15°, 4 minutes = 1°)
Deviation of actual time zones from the theoretical 15° grid due to political/economic reasons
UTC offset range: UTC-12 to UTC+14 (not a symmetric ±12 — UPSC trap)
Half-hour and quarter-hour offset anomalies (India UTC+5:30, Nepal UTC+5:45, Iran UTC+3:30)

concepts.name: Indian Standard Time (IST): Basis and Anomalies
key_dimensions: IST = UTC+5:30, based on 82.5°E meridian passing through Mirzapur/Naini near Allahabad
India has a single time zone despite ~30° longitudinal extent (sunrise difference of ~2 hours between east and west)
Debate on having two time zones for India — arguments for/against
IST does not observe Daylight Saving Time (DST) — implications for trade and aviation

concepts.name: International Date Line (IDL): Location and Definition
key_dimensions: Approximately follows 180° meridian but deviates significantly to avoid land masses
Crossing IDL eastward: date goes back one day; westward: date advances one day
IDL is not defined by international treaty — it is a geographic convention (UPSC trap)
Distinction between 180° meridian (geographic line) and IDL (functional, irregular line)

concepts.name: Deviations of IDL from 180° Meridian: Geopolitical Reasons
key_dimensions: Eastward deviation around Siberia/Chukotka (Russia) to keep Russia in one date
Westward deviation around Aleutian Islands (USA) to keep Alaska in one date
Major 2011 Samoa shift: Samoa and Tokelau moved IDL west of them to align with Australia/NZ trading partners
Kiribati's extreme eastward extension of time zone to UTC+14 to remain in one date — largest UTC offset

concepts.name: Coordinated Universal Time (UTC): Standard and Offset System
key_dimensions: UTC as the global time standard based on International Atomic Time (TAI) with leap second adjustments
UTC replaced GMT as the international civil time standard (GMT is now a time zone, not a standard)
UTC+14 (Line Islands, Kiribati) is the most advanced; UTC-12 (Baker/Howland Islands, US) is the most behind
Countries spanning multiple UTC offsets: Russia (11 zones), USA (6 zones), France (12 zones including territories — UPSC trap for 'most time zones'

concepts.name: Daylight Saving Time (DST): Mechanism and Global Practice
key_dimensions: Clocks advanced by 1 hour in summer to maximize daylight — observed mainly in temperate regions
Countries NOT observing DST: India, China, Japan, most of Africa, most of Southeast Asia
DST creates temporary changes in UTC offset (e.g., UK moves from UTC+0 to UTC+1 in summer)
Impact on time difference calculations between DST-observing and non-observing countries — examination trap

concepts.name: Countries with Single Time Zone Despite Large Longitudinal Extent
key_dimensions: China uses a single time zone (UTC+8) despite spanning ~5 theoretical time zones — political unification rationale
India: single time zone despite ~30° span — contrast with China's approach
Consequences: extreme sunrise/sunset times in western China (Xinjiang) — social and economic impacts
Comparison: USA and Russia use multiple time zones as counter-examples

concepts.name: Countries/Territories with the Most Time Zones
key_dimensions: France has the most time zones (~12) due to overseas territories — UPSC trap (not Russia or USA)
Russia has 11 time zones (largest country by area but not most time zones)
USA has 6 standard time zones (9 including territories)
Australia has 3 standard + 2 half-hour offset zones — notable for internal half-hour anomalies

concepts.name: Half-Hour and Quarter-Hour Offset Time Zones: Global Anomalies
key_dimensions: Nepal (UTC+5:45) — only country with a quarter-hour offset, based on Kathmandu's longitude
India (UTC+5:30), Iran (UTC+3:30), Afghanistan (UTC+4:30), Sri Lanka (UTC+5:30)
Australia: South Australia (UTC+9:30), Lord Howe Island (UTC+10:30)
Reason for non-standard offsets: political decisions to differentiate from neighbours or geographic centrality

concepts.name: Relationship Between Longitude and Local Time: Calculation Principles
key_dimensions: Earth rotates 360° in 24 hours → 15° per hour → 1° per 4 minutes
Places east of a reference meridian are ahead in time; west are behind
Calculating time at a location given its longitude and a reference time — standard exam calculation type
Difference between local mean time (based on exact longitude) and standard time (based on standard meridian)

concepts.name: The 1884 International Meridian Conference: Outcomes and Significance
key_dimensions: Held in Washington D.C.; Greenwich adopted as Prime Meridian by 22 of 25 nations
France abstained (used Paris Meridian until 1911) — notable exception
Established the foundation for international time zones and standard time
Significance for navigation, telegraphy, and railways — practical drivers of standardization

concepts.name: Samoa Time Zone Shift (2011): Case Study in IDL Adjustment
key_dimensions: Samoa skipped December 29, 2011 entirely to move from UTC-11 to UTC+13
Motivation: align business hours with Australia and New Zealand (major trading partners)
American Samoa (US territory) did not shift — now 25 hours behind (not 1 hour ahead as before)
Demonstrates that IDL and time zones are political/economic decisions, not just geographic ones

concepts.name: Kiribati and UTC+14: Easternmost Time Zone
key_dimensions: Kiribati extended its time zone to UTC+14 in 1995 to keep all islands in the same date
Line Islands (part of Kiribati) are the first place on Earth to experience each new day/New Year
UTC+14 lies east of the IDL — demonstrating IDL and UTC are independent systems (key UPSC trap)
Caroline Island (Millennium Island) renamed in 2000 to mark being 'first' for the new millennium

concepts.name: Antimeridian (180° Meridian): Properties and Distinction from IDL
key_dimensions: 180° meridian is the theoretical antimeridian of Greenwich, exactly opposite the Prime Meridian
Passes through the Pacific Ocean, Fiji, Russia (Chukotka), Antarctica
IDL deviates from 180° but the 180° meridian itself has no legal or official date-change function
Fiji straddles 180° but uses a single time zone (UTC+12) — IDL placed west of Fiji

concepts.name: Time Zone Implications for International Aviation and Commerce
key_dimensions: Aviation uses UTC (Zulu time) to avoid confusion across time zones
Flight duration vs. clock time difference — crossing the IDL can make arrival appear before departure by calendar
Business time overlap windows between major financial centers (New York, London, Tokyo, Mumbai)
Scheduling anomalies: flights from USA to Asia crossing IDL gain/lose a calendar day

concepts.name: Arctic and Antarctic Time Zones: Special Cases
key_dimensions: At the poles, all meridians converge — no meaningful local time based on longitude
Antarctic research stations use the time of their supply country (e.g., India's Maitri uses IST)
McMurdo Station (US) uses New Zealand time for logistical convenience
North Pole has no permanent settlement — Arctic nations' time zones extend theoretically to the pole

concepts.name: China's UTC+8 Single Time Zone Policy: Geopolitical and Social Implications
key_dimensions: Adopted after 1949 to promote national unity — replaced 5 pre-existing time zones
Xinjiang (westernmost) has unofficial 'Xinjiang time' (UTC+6) used locally — dual time system in practice
Solar noon in Xinjiang occurs around 3 PM official time — extreme mismatch
Comparison with India's single time zone policy — both prioritize unity over geographic accuracy

concepts.name: Leap Seconds and UTC: Relationship with Earth's Rotation
key_dimensions: Earth's rotation is gradually slowing — UTC periodically adds leap seconds to stay within 0.9 seconds of UT1
27 leap seconds added since 1972 — last added in December 2016
Decision to abolish leap seconds by 2035 (ITU resolution) — implications for GPS and atomic timekeeping
Distinction: leap second (timekeeping adjustment) vs. leap year (calendar adjustment) — UPSC conceptual trap

concepts.name: Greenwich Mean Time (GMT) vs. UTC: Modern Distinction
key_dimensions: GMT was the world standard until 1972 when UTC (based on atomic clocks) replaced it officially
GMT is now technically a time zone (UTC+0) used by UK in winter; UTC is the standard
In casual/legal usage, GMT and UTC are often treated as equivalent — but differ by up to 0.9 seconds
UK uses GMT in winter and BST (British Summer Time, UTC+1) in summer — common UPSC confusion point
